agree.reason: The script is respectful and puts the July closure of my own branch first, but as a fixed-income homeowner who voted no last time, I'm told I'll pay about $120 a year and get nothing that makes that sum feel small or worth it, so it may not change my vote.

honest.reason: The arithmetic is correct ($640k → $121.60/yr; $500k → $95; a 48–52 loss is a 4-point margin), and the script rightly drops the 'cup of coffee' line, which is false for Ridgeview. But 'using the library more than ever' claims more than the 22%-since-2021 figure supports.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the Ridgeview cost and a do-it-yourself formula, but it never uses the $2.3M a year raised or a per-day figure (about 33 cents). The fixed-income example uses a $500k home, which tells a Ridgeview owner nothing about their own bill.

right_comparison.reason: It clearly sets out the alternative (the Ridgeview branch closes in July and Sunday hours stay gone) alongside the rise in visits, though it doesn't spell out the cost of losing the branch next to the $10 a month.

qualification.reason: A persuasive door script with a stated rate, a stated term and a dated consequence doesn't need any hedging.

objections.reason: The 'blank check' charge from the president's letter gets a solid answer (fixed rate, six-year end, named uses), but the fixed-income reply just hands over a formula and a lower-value example without addressing whether the cost is affordable.

fit.reason: The main pitch runs about 60–75 seconds and the whole thing plausibly fits on one card with its rebuttals. It leaves out the requested coffee comparison, which is the right call because the figures make it untrue.
